requirements.requirement: Remote ingress rejects unauthenticated MCP requests.
Executor exposes full Desktop Commander workstation semantics without a bounded executable or argument-grant mode.
Default per-device capacity is 8 parallel execution lanes.
Default upstream capacity is 64 parallel logic lanes.
Tunnel profile allows at least 64 concurrent upstream requests.
Connection generation changes on device replacement and stale generations cannot dispatch effects.
Post-dispatch timeout or disconnect is classified OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never silently replayed.
Operator tunnel/API credentials remain external to repository source.
Repository source, deployed tunnel, connected device, and observed workstation effect remain separate evidence classes.
A device ID with a configured per-device token accepts only that token; a shared fallback token cannot impersonate the mapped device.

Windows runtime start/stop/restart/status scripts preserve 8/64 defaults, do not persist runtime credentials, fence recorded PIDs by command-line identity before termination, and require the tunnel client's live /readyz state for a running status.
All checked-in PowerShell operator scripts parse successfully on Windows CI.
Windows runtime captures the tunnel client's per-run health URL and re-probes /readyz instead of treating a surviving tunnel process as current readiness.
Unauthenticated health probes expose aggregate readiness/capacity state but not connected workstation identities; detailed device inventory requires the Executor client bearer.

Installer and real-payload qualifier preseed the pinned @vscode/ripgrep release cache via a direct release asset and verify its SHA-256 before rebuild, without importing the WorkBridge bounded process overlay.

An explicit operator-run live-tunnel qualifier requires a non-loopback HTTPS remote MCP URL, drives 64 remote MCP calls, and requires observed overlap of at least 8 execution lanes and 64 logic lanes; ordinary CI does not claim this live deployment evidence.

The pinned Desktop Commander payload preserves ordinary workstation environment context but does not inherit Executor/tunnel credentials or loader-injection variables; Windows real-payload qualification verifies an EXECUTOR_* sentinel cannot reach a start_process child.
